newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower, ignores stock expectation.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower, ignores stock expectation.

text.p: COMEX copper ended lower despite market expectations for further drawdowns in LME stocks on Tuesday against a background of protracted labor talks at key U.S. production plants.
Activity was dulled by the U.S. Columbus Day holiday.
Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities said LME stocks were expected to fall a further 3,000 to 4,000 tonnes Tuesday, but the market was not responding.
"The market is only responding to the negative news such as the Sumitomo ripple effect. Fundamentals are secondary at the moment. There is unease overall," Raptopoulos said.
December COMEX settled down 1.40 cents at 90.10 cents a lb after trading from 91.45 to 90.00 cents. Spot October went out 1.65 cents lower at 91.50 cents.

Labor talks at Kennecott Copper in Utah covering 1,800 union members, will resume on Tuesday, a Kennecott spokeswoman said. The previous three-year contract expired on September 30 but the refinery was operating normally.

Labor talks at Phelps Dodge's Chino mine were expected to resume towards the end of October, company officials have said. Chino, in New Mexico, is also operating normally despite the labor contract there expiring at the end of June.
